extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners working on personalized news recommender systems (NLP, recommender-systems, data mining), and platform engineers/policy researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, evaluating, and improving personalized news recommender systems, covering modeling of news and users, ranking, fairness, privacy, robustness, diversity, and societal impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity is critical for personalized news recommendation; users may not prefer to click news with homogeneous information and improving the information variety is important for user experience and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing methods mostly optimize accuracy while ignoring diversity; some methods recommend news diverse from previously clicked news or diversify the top list. Many diversity-aware methods rely on reranking, which may not achieve an optimal tradeoff between accuracy and diversity. Further research should learn unified diversity-aware models rather than post-hoc reranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content Moderation (avoid low-quality/harmful content)
rubrics_metrics.description: News recommendation systems should avoid recommending clickbaits, fake news, misinformation, adversarially constructed items, and content that is low-quality or harmful (e.g., racialism and hate speech).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manual moderation is infeasible at scale; leverage signals such as high ratios of short dwell time (e.g., <10s) as clickbait indicators, and user behaviors like comments and social sharing to detect misinformation and harmful content. Incorporate user feedback and content-quality detectors (fake-news and clickbait detection) into recommendation pipelines to improve responsibility and avoid societal harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep News Understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: News modeling requires deep understanding of textual content and multimodal information (images, videos, slides) and of non-content factors such as publisher, popularity and recency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advanced NLP (e.g., knowledge-aware pre-trained language models) and multimodal content modeling to capture complementary signals; build a unified framework that incorporates property features and context features and models relatedness between them to improve downstream user modeling and ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal User Modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: User modeling must comprehensively infer user interests from multiple kinds of behaviors and feedback, represent diverse multi-grained interests, and capture dynamics over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on click signals (they are noisy/sparse); incorporate other behaviors (read, dislike, comments, sharing). Use richer user representations (embedding sets, graphs) rather than a single embedding. Apply advanced sequence modeling techniques to capture evolving interests and relations across time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective and Efficient Personalized Ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Ranking should accurately target user interests while being computationally efficient and mindful of long-term user engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coarse-grained relevance between candidate news and user interest may be insufficient; fine-grained relatedness models exist but can be inefficient. Research should develop methods that are both effective and efficient. Additionally, ranking must trade off accuracy and diversity to avoid filter bubbles, and move beyond greedy, short-sighted ranking policies toward strategies that optimize long-term rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbolic Representation Learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Representations for users and news learned in Euclidean space may fail to capture inherent hierarchical structures in the data (user interest hierarchies, topics, knowledge graphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore hyperbolic representation learning (e.g., hyperbolic attention, hyperbolic GCN) and architectures that better capture hierarchical relations; leverage prior successes in CF and knowledge graph embedding to improve matching and modeling in recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified Model Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Model training should integrate diverse supervision and be robust and adaptive rather than relying only on click signals or fragile manual tuning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Incorporate multiple supervised and self-supervised objectives beyond clicks to improve signal quality. 2) Adopt self-adaptive multi-task learning to automatically tune loss coefficients instead of manual tuning. 3) Use more informative negative sampling methods (random negatives can be noisy). 4) Combine offline and online learning to reduce performance drift when deploying models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Context Integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Social interactions (comments, replies, sharing) are informative for user modeling and content understanding and can reflect opinions, preferences, satisfaction, content quality, and authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate social-context signals to improve accuracy, timeliness (e.g., breaking news detection), and content-quality assessment. This area is currently under-explored and can provide rich complementary information for recommender systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy-preserving News Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Protecting user privacy is essential; methods like federated learning are explored but have specific challenges in the news recommendation context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key challenges include efficient online deployment of federated models, privacy risks during training/serving, and the heavy utility cost of canonical differential privacy techniques. Data isolation in federated settings also hinders access to context features like CTR and collaborative information (e.g., for GNNs). Develop effective, efficient privacy-preserving approaches that balance utility and privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security and Robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: News recommender systems face security threats such as poisoning attacks, backdoors, adversarial examples, and vulnerabilities amplified in federated settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research is needed on defenses and robust algorithms to ensure stability and reliability. Consider threat models for both malicious users and untrusted infrastructure and evaluate robustness under poisoning/adversarial scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity-aware News Recommendation (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond generic diversity, there are three concrete diversity directions: temporal-spatial diversity, personalized diversity preferences, and fine-grained diversity across many attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) Temporal-spatial diversity: recommend items diverse from each other and from historical clicks. 2) Personalized diversity: adapt the diversity–accuracy tradeoff per user. 3) Fine-grained diversity: diversify across content, topic, publishers, locations, opinions and emotions. Research should address all three to improve perceived quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias-free (Debiased) News Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Biases in user behavior data propagate to models and can be amplified; debiasing is essential for accurate and robust recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand influences of different bias types on behavior and models; consider per-user differences in how biases act; develop unified debiasing frameworks that can reduce effects of multiple biases simultaneously while maintaining accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness-aware News Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness requires providing equitable recommendation services to different user groups and giving fair exposure/opportunities to different news providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research directions include reducing consumer-side unfairness related to sensitive attributes (current approaches like adversarial learning are brittle), balancing provider-side fairness across diverse providers (topic preference, reputation), and achieving multi-side fairness without heavy accuracy loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content-quality-aware Recommendation (learning from user feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn to recommend high-quality news by leveraging user feedback signals (comments, dislikes) and auxiliary detectors, even without extra labeled moderation resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate content-moderation tasks (fake-news detection, clickbait detection) into recommendation models or use user feedback as guidance to build content-quality-aware recommenders that avoid promoting harmful or low-quality content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal Impact Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized news recommenders can influence users' opinions and produce large-scale societal effects (political, economic, psychological).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should identify and analyze these impacts (e.g., influence on political events, economic activities, psychological health) and develop methods to reduce potential negative societal outcomes of personalization.
